objective: Implement Ruling D53 phase 1: an optional recompute tier, typed results on the answer, a recompute node of three blind samples, a free recompute_vote check, and a new workflow answer-and-recompute whose flag is a note on the delivery. Free work; no paid call.
evidence: Ruling D53: docs/reviews/2026-10-18-d53-the-recompute-vote.md, §2 (the ruling, items 1 to 6), §4 (limits), §6 (not ruled).
The measured vote: evals/tier4/probes/recompute_vote.py (the majority rule) and evals/tier4/probes/recompute_check.py (ident, TOL = 0.03, parse_table).

The recorded answers and samples, in docs/traces/: the pilot 20261018T022735Z-tier4-pilot-batch2.jsonl (05e5f56f); the calibrations 20261018T034225Z (batch 3), 20261018T164435Z (batch 4), 20261018T180951Z (batch 5), 20261018T185019Z (batch 6); the vote samples 20261018T035714Z, 20261018T164638Z, 20261018T181158Z, 20261018T192122Z; the T4-42 repeats 20261018T193358Z-repeat-T4-42.json (33c1e1c2).
The skip precedent: autornd/graph/adapter.py _phase_doublecheck (Ruling D48 (3): a check that did not run carries no approval-shaped value).
The workflow precedent: workflows/verify-first.yaml (triage, asks, asks_anchored, context, one implement with no plan, blocked_check, blocked_gate, coverage and consistency as notes).

include: autornd/config.py: model_recompute (optional tier, ships empty) and recompute_max_tokens (default 32768, with a comment citing the tier-4 vote samples)
autornd/engine/phases.py: run_recompute; the implement prompt's results instruction
autornd/graph/checks.py: @check('recompute_vote') and its private identity helper
tests/test_recompute_vote.py (new) and the fixtures it reads
HANDOVER.md, README.md, AGENTS.md: counts and the new workflow and tier
exclude: evals/: frozen batches, keys and scorers; the probes are read-only references
autornd/database.py: no schema change (hard rule 12). If one is needed, STOP and report

constraints: FREE. No paid call. Every test is provider-free, and the network guard stays at 0.

TIER: model_recompute is optional, like model_premium. Importing autornd with it unset works. When it is unset, _phase_recompute returns {skipped: true, flagged: false, reason: <plain sentence>} and makes no call. recompute_vote reads a skip as skipped, never as passed.

RESULTS: ResultValue = {ask: str, value: float | str, unit: str = ''}. ImplementVerdict.results: list[ResultValue] defaults to empty. A null results field coerces to empty, and a null unit to ''. Existing recorded ImplementVerdicts must still parse.

IMPLEMENT PROMPT, in answer-and-recompute only: after the asks, add 'In results, give one entry for each ask of kind value or verdict listed above: ask = its number, value = the final number or the identifier you chose, unit = the unit of the number (empty for an identifier). These are the values your summary states.' Gate the addition on the node's args (for example args: {results: true}), so engineering-rnd and verify-first prompts stay byte-identical.
RECOMPUTE NODE: args {samples: 3}, declared in YAML. Each sample is one separate call on the recompute tier.

RECOMPUTE PROMPT: system 'You are a careful senior engineer.' User: the request; the grounding context; the anchored asks of kind value and verdict, numbered as in the answer; then 'Compute the answer yourself. Return JSON with results: one entry per listed ask, {ask: its number, value: your final number or the identifier you chose, unit: the unit of the number, empty for an identifier}.'
RECOMPUTE ISOLATION: no sample's messages contain the implement summary, its results, the plan or another sample's output.
ACCOUNTING: each sample goes through the client's reservation path, which reserves its worst case and releases it by identity (D45, D47). Add no new post site.

VOTE: identity values compare after dropping case, spacing and punctuation, with '×' and a count's 'x' read as a separator (recompute_check.ident without its 'in parallel' special case). Numbers compare within relative tolerance 0.03, only when the units are equal after normalise_key; otherwise the ask is no_consensus. The majority is a value matched by >= 2 of the samples that answered the ask. A disagreement is a majority that differs from the answer. flagged = at least one disagreement. Fewer than 2 parseable samples, or no answer result naming an anchored ask, makes the vote unchecked with flagged false. Output: flagged, skipped, unchecked, disagreements [{ask, answer, majority, support}], no_consensus [ask], samples_parsed.
FLAG = NOTE: the vote never blocks, routes or revises, and the run's status is decided without it. The vote's output is in the run's outputs and in the delivery the API returns.
NEVER PARSE ENGLISH: the vote reads typed fields only.
A defect found in existing harness code while doing this is a STOP-and-report, not a fix.
acceptance_criteria: (a) Schema. ImplementVerdict without results parses (results == []); with null results parses to []; ResultValue with a null unit parses to ''. Break-proof: make results required and a recorded verdict from docs/traces fails to parse.

(b) Skip. With model_recompute unset, a mocked answer-and-recompute run makes zero recompute calls, and the vote is {skipped: true, flagged: false}. Break-proof: return flagged-false-and-not-skipped from the skip branch and the test fails.

(c) Isolation. Mocked: every recompute sample's system and user messages contain neither the implement summary nor any results value string. Break-proof: append the summary to the recompute message and the test fails.

(d) Accounting. Mocked client: three samples make three reservations, each released by its own identity. A sample that fails after dispatch keeps its own worst case as unreconciled liability. Break-proof shown.

(e) The vote on real recorded answers. Build a fixture from docs/traces: each tier-4 answer the records scored, converted to ResultValue lists with recompute_check.parse_table and the probe's KEY_ROWS, and the matching vote samples. At least: kimi's T4-42 calibration answer and repeat 3 (wrong); F's T4-15 from the pilot (wrong); the batch-3 four and the batch-4, batch-5 and batch-6 kimi answers (correct); the T4-42 repeats 1 and 2 (correct). The check's flags match recompute_vote.score's on each answer. That includes repeat 1's false flag on the ambiguous row 'current compared with I_n', recorded in D53 §1: the check reproduces it rather than hiding it. If an answer the records name cannot be found in docs/traces, STOP and report which.

(f) Vote rules, unit tests: identity normalisation ('VL-42' == 'vl 42'); the 3% tolerance edge (2.9% agrees, 3.1% disagrees); a unit mismatch gives no_consensus, not a flag; a 1-1-1 split gives no_consensus; 1 parseable sample gives unchecked. Each rule with a break-proof.

(g) Workflow. workflows/answer-and-recompute.yaml loads. A mocked run delivers with the vote in its outputs: once flagged (the answer differs from a 2-of-3 majority), once not. In both, the run's status equals that of a run with the vote nodes removed.
(h) Unchanged: engineering-rnd and verify-first implement prompts are byte-identical to main's (a test compares rendered prompts), and every existing test passes unmodified.
(i) Docs: .env.example carries MODEL_RECOMPUTE= empty; tests/test_docs.py passes (no model names). Counts re-derived from pytest --collect-only in HANDOVER.md, README.md and AGENTS.md.
(j) Suite green before and after, network guard 0, CI 5/5, PR opened.

verification.expected: All pass; network guard: 0; report the count before and after.

rollback: Revert the PR. Nothing outside the new workflow, the optional tier and the default-empty results field changes behaviour.
deliverable: One PR: the tier, schemas, node, check, workflow, prompts, tests with their break-proofs, docs and counts, and the response DONE. Then STOP. Routing on a flag waits on D53 §7.
assumptions: The client can make three separate calls within one node. If a node can return only one ModelResponse, record all three in the phase's response list the way rosters do. If neither works, STOP and report.
The API's delivery carries the run's outputs. If it does not, add only the vote's output to it and say so in deviations.
